'''Microsoft Advertising''', also known as '''Microsoft Ads'''  (formerly '''Bing Ads''') is an online advertising platform developed by Microsoft, where advertisers bid to display brief advertisements to web users. It provides [[pay per click]] advertising on search engines [[Microsoft Bing|Bing]], [[Yahoo! Search|Yahoo!]] and [[DuckDuckGo]], as well as on other websites, mobile apps, and videos.

Advertisers can import their Google Ads campaigns directly into the Microsoft Advertising platform. This time saving feature encourages advertisers to use their platform even though it has significantly less users.

In 2021, Microsoft Advertising surpassed US$10 billion in annual revenue.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Microsoft's ad revenue hit $10B, and it's investing — is it a sleeping giant about to wake?|url = https://digiday.com/media/microsofts-ad-revenue-hit-10b-and-its-investing-is-a-sleeping-giant-about-to-wake/|website = DIGIDAY|access-date = 2022-06-12}}</ref>

==History==
Microsoft was the last of the "big three" [[search engine]]s (which also includes [[Google]] and [[Yahoo!]]) to develop its own system for delivering [[pay-per-click]] (PPC) ads.  Until the beginning of 2006, all of the ads displayed on the MSN Search engine were supplied by Overture (and later Yahoo!).  MSN collected a portion of the ad revenue in return for displaying Yahoo!'s ads on its search engine.<ref>
{{cite news
|url=http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/businesstechnology/2002970721_microsoft04.html
|title=Microsoft's adCenter is Google, Yahoo! rival
|publisher=The Seattle Times
|access-date=2008-01-12
|last=Peterson
|first=Kim
| date=2006-05-04
}}
</ref>

As search marketing grew, Microsoft began developing its own system, MSN adCenter, for selling PPC advertisements directly to advertisers.  As the system was phased in, MSN Search (now [[Bing (search engine)|Bing]]) showed Yahoo! and adCenter advertising in its search results.  Microsoft effort to create AdCenter was led by Tarek Najm, then general manager of the MSN division of Microsoft. In June 2006, the contract between Yahoo! and Microsoft expired and Microsoft was displaying only ads from adCenter until 2010.

{{Internet Marketing}}

In November 2006 Microsoft acquired Deep Metrix, a company situated in Gatineau, Canada, that created web-analytics software. Microsoft has built a new product adCenter Analytics based on the acquired technology. In October, 2007 the beta version of Microsoft Project Gatineau was released to a limited number of participants.<ref>{{cite web

In May 2007, Microsoft agreed to purchase the [[digital marketing]] solutions parent company, [[aQuantive]], for roughly $6 billion.<ref>

|url=https://techcrunch.com/2007/05/18/microsoft-pays-6-billion-for-aquantive/

</ref> Microsoft later resold Atlas, a key piece of the aQuantive acquisition, to Facebook in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://allthingsd.com/20130228/sold-finally-facebook-takes-atlas-from-microsoft-so-it-can-get-serious-about-ads/|title = Sold! (Finally) Facebook Takes Atlas from Microsoft, So It Can Get Serious About Ads}}</ref>

Microsoft acquired [[ScreenTonic]] on May 3, 2007,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.clickz.com/showPage.html?page=3625762 |title=Microsoft Acquires European Mobile Ad Firm - ClickZ<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=2008-04-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080507185333/http://www.clickz.com/showPage.html?page=3625762 |archive-date=2008-05-07 |url-status=dead }}</ref> AdECN on July 26, 2007,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2007-07-26 |title=Microsoft to Acquire AdECN, Inc. |url=https://news.microsoft.com/2007/07/26/microsoft-to-acquire-adecn-inc/ |access-date=2022-11-23 |website=Stories |language=en-US}}</ref> and YaData on February 27, 2008, and merged their technologies into adCenter.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schonfeld |first=Erick |date=2008-02-27 |title=Microsoft Picks Up Israeli Ad-Targetting Software Startup YaData for a Reported $20 Million to $30 Million |url=https://techcrunch.com/2008/02/27/microsoft-picks-up-israeli-ad-targetting-software-startup-yadata-for-a-reported-20-million-to-30-million/ |access-date=2022-11-23 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}</ref>

On February 23, 2009, the Publisher Leadership Council was created under the umbrella of Microsoft Advertising. The council was responsible for delivering the next-generation advertising platform for the publishers of digital media resulting in the formation of [[Microsoft pubCenter]].<ref>[http://www.microsoft.com/presspass/press/2009/feb09/02-23PublisherAdCouncilPR.mspx?rss_fdn=Press%20Releases Microsoft Advertising Announces Formation of Publisher Leadership Council], February 23, 2009, News Press Release, Microsoft</ref>

In January 2010, Microsoft announced a deal in which it would take over the functional operation of Yahoo! Search, and set up a joint venture to sell advertising on both Yahoo! Search and [[Bing (search engine)|Bing]] known as the Microsoft Search Alliance. A complete transition of all Yahoo! sponsored ad clients to Microsoft adCenter occurred in October 2010.<ref name="Microsoft and Yahoo seal web deal ">{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/8174763.stm |title=Microsoft and Yahoo seal web deal |publisher=BBC News |date=2009-07-29 |access-date=2012-11-10}}</ref>

On September 10, 2012, adCenter was renamed to '''Bing Ads''', and the Search Alliance was renamed the Yahoo! Bing Network.<ref name=zdnet-bingads>{{cite web|last=Foley|first=Mary Jo|title=Microsoft gives Yahoo name top billing in Microsoft advertising rebrand|url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/microsoft-gives-yahoo-name-top-billing-in-microsoft-advertising-rebrand/|work=ZDnet|access-date=10 September 2012}}</ref>

In April 2015, the Yahoo! partnership was modified; Yahoo! Search will only have to feature Bing results on the "majority" of desktop traffic, leaving the company open to "enhance the search experience" non-exclusively on both desktop and mobile. Additionally, Microsoft will take over as the exclusive seller of ads delivered through Bing. Yahoo! will sell its own ads through its new in-house Gemini platform.<ref name=ars-april2015deal>{{cite web|title=Microsoft loses exclusivity in shaken up Yahoo search deal|url=https://arstechnica.com/information-technology/2015/04/microsoft-loses-exclusivity-in-shaken-up-yahoo-search-deal/|website=Ars Technica|date=16 April 2015|access-date=30 June 2015}}</ref><ref name=tc-changes>{{cite web|title=Ad Tech And Mobile In Focus In Microsoft And Yahoo's Renewed Search Deal|url=https://techcrunch.com/2015/04/16/microsoft-and-yahoo-renew-search-allian/|website=TechCrunch|access-date=30 June 2015}}</ref>

On June 29, 2015, [[AOL Inc.]] announced a deal and partnership to take over the majority of Microsoft's ad sales business. Under the pact, AOL will take over the sale of display, video, and mobile ads on various Microsoft platforms in nine countries, including Brazil, Canada, the United States, and the United Kingdom. As many as 1200 Microsoft employees involved with the business will be transferred to AOL. In turn, AOL's properties will replace Google Search with Bing, and display Bing Ads sold by Microsoft.<ref name=nyt-aolads>{{cite news|title=AOL in Deal With Microsoft to Take Over Display Ad Business|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/06/30/business/aol-in-deal-with-microsoft-to-take-over-display-ad-business.html?_r=0|access-date=30 June 2015|work=The New York Times}}</ref><ref name=wsj-bingaolads>{{cite news|title=AOL Takes Over Majority of Microsoft's Ad Business, Swaps Google Search For Bing|url=https://blogs.wsj.com/cmo/2015/06/29/aol-takes-over-majority-of-microsofts-ad-business-swaps-google-search-for-bing/|access-date=30 June 2015|work=Wall Street Journal}}</ref>

In May 2018, Bing Ads released additional productivity and time-saving tools for users managing their campaigns via Bing Ads Editor.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://searchengineland.com/bing-ads-editor-adds-new-features-for-apple-users-298551|title=Bing Ads Editor adds labels for Mac users & other features for Windows users - Search Engine Land|date=2018-05-17|work=Search Engine Land|access-date=2018-06-13|language=en-US}}</ref>

On April 30, 2019, Bing Ads was re-branded to Microsoft Advertising.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://app.beebom.com/bing-ads-re-branded-microsoft-advertising/|title=Bing Ads Re-branded to Microsoft Advertising|date=2019-04-30|website=Beebom|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-30|archive-date=2019-04-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190430180017/https://app.beebom.com/bing-ads-re-branded-microsoft-advertising/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On August 5, 2019, Microsoft acquired '''PromoteIQ''', a leading provider of vendor marketing technology to online retailers and brands.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://about.ads.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/post/august-2019/microsoft-acquires-promoteiq|title=PromoteIQ acquired by Microsoft|date=2019-08-05|website=Microsoft|language=en-US|access-date=2022-06-12}}</ref>

On December 21, 2021, Microsoft announced its plans to acquire [[Xandr]] from AT&T. Six months later, Microsoft disclosed that the acquisition had been completed.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://searchengineland.com/microsoft-atts-xandr-acquisition-complete-385631|title=Microsoft, AT&T's Xandr acquisition complete|date=2022-06-06|website=Search Engine Land|language=en-US|access-date=2022-06-12}}</ref>

In May 2025, Microsoft confirmed that it would sunset its Invest DSP (formerly known as Xandr). As reported by [[Digiday]], the decision to end its DSP operations was driven by the company's AI priorities: "Our commitment to more private and personalized advertising experiences for a conversational and agentic world is not achievable with the industry’s current DSP model and, therefore, it no longer aligns with our investment in this future."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shields |first=Ronan |date=2025-05-14 |title=Microsoft Advertising is closing the Xandr DSP, layoffs pending |url=https://digiday.com/media-buying/microsoft-advertising-is-closing-the-xandr-dsp/ |access-date=2026-04-10 |website=Digiday |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Technology==
Similar to [[Google Ads]], Microsoft Advertising uses both the maximum amount an advertiser is willing to [[pay-per-click]] (PPC) on their ad and the advertisement's [[click-through rate]] (CTR) to determine how frequently an advertisement is shown.  This system encourages advertisers to write effective ads and to advertise only on searches which are relevant to their advertisement.

In 2021, Microsoft Advertising began rolling out LinkedIn audience observation and bid management targeting, allowing advertisers to monitor and bid against common LinkedIn Ads audiences, including company size, industry, job function, as well as lists of individual companies.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Microsoft Ads LinkedIn Account Targeting |url=https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/ad-targeting/account-targeting?trk=nw_ml_at}}</ref>

Similar to [[AdWords Editor|Google Ads Editor]], Microsoft Advertising provides a desktop tool to manage campaigns offline, called Microsoft Ads Editor.  Using this editor you can make offline changes to your campaigns and later sync it online.

Microsoft Advertising also provides [[API]]s that can be used to manage advertising campaigns.
